items.note: landmark: distal medial projection of SRC_Z_TIBIA_R/_L
items.custom_note: Distal medial projection of the tibia (below the level of the ankle mortise roof), both sides.

items.section: Bones and Landmarks > Skeletal framework
items.note: landmarks: head and neck at proximal end of SRC_Z_FIBULA_R/_L
items.custom_note: Narrow segment just below the fibular head, where the common fibular nerve winds round, both sides.

items.section: Bones and Landmarks > Skeletal framework
items.note: landmark: distal end of SRC_Z_FIBULA_R/_L
items.custom_note: Distal end of the fibula, lower and more posterior than the medial malleolus, both sides.

items.section: Bones and Landmarks > Tarsal bones
items.note: talus exists; head/neck/body/trochlea are regions of SRC_Z_TALUS_R/_L
items.custom_note: Superior articular surface of the talar body, gripped by the tibia (found as the upward talar surface facing the tibia), both sides.

items.section: Bones and Landmarks > Tarsal bones
items.note: calcaneus exists; tuberosity is the posterior region of SRC_Z_CALCANEUS_R/_L
items.custom_note: Posterior end of the calcaneus (heel; Achilles insertion, medial and lateral processes), both sides; appended to the calcaneus.

items.section: Bones and Landmarks > Tarsal bones
items.note: navicular exists; tuberosity is its medial plantar projection
items.custom_note: Medial (plantar-directed) projection of the navicular, main insertion of tibialis posterior, both sides; appended to the navicular.

Ankle and Foot Joints and Supporting Structures
items.note: medial malleolus of SRC_Z_TIBIA_* fanning to SRC_Z_NAVICULAR_BONE_*, SRC_Z_TALUS_*, sustentaculum of SRC_Z_CALCANEUS_*
items.custom_note: Strong triangular medial collateral ligament fanning from the medial malleolus to the navicular (tuberosity), the talar neck, the sustentaculum tali of the calcaneus and the posterior talus (tibionavicular, tibiospring, tibiocalcaneal, tibiotalar parts); both sides.

items.section: Ankle and Foot Joints and Supporting Structures
items.note: lateral malleolus of SRC_Z_FIBULA_* to neck of SRC_Z_TALUS_*
items.custom_note: Flat band from the anterior margin of the lateral malleolus anteromedially to the lateral neck of the talus; weakest lateral ligament, first torn in inversion sprains; both sides.

items.section: Ankle and Foot Joints and Supporting Structures
items.note: tip of lateral malleolus (SRC_Z_FIBULA_*) to lateral SRC_Z_CALCANEUS_*
items.custom_note: Cord from the tip of the lateral malleolus down and back to the lateral surface of the calcaneus (deep to the fibular tendons); both sides.

items.section: Ankle and Foot Joints and Supporting Structures
items.note: malleolar fossa of SRC_Z_FIBULA_* to posterior process of SRC_Z_TALUS_*
items.custom_note: Thick band running horizontally from the malleolar fossa of the lateral malleolus medially and back to the lateral tubercle of the posterior process of the talus; strongest of the lateral ligaments; both sides.

items.section: Ankle and Foot Joints and Supporting Structures
items.note: bony arches: medial (SRC_Z_CALCANEUS_*, TALUS, NAVICULAR, cuneiforms, metatarsals I-III), lateral (calcaneus, SRC_Z_CUBOID_BONE_*, metatarsals IV-V)
items.custom_note: Schematic arch line traced just under the medial column (calcaneus, talus, navicular = keystone, medial cuneiform, metatarsal I) from the heel to the first metatarsal head: the higher, more mobile arch; both sides.

items.section: Ankle and Foot Joints and Supporting Structures
items.note: bony arch across cuneiforms (SRC_Z_*_CUNEIFORM_BONE_*), SRC_Z_CUBOID_BONE_* and metatarsal bases
items.custom_note: Schematic arch line traced across the plantar surfaces of the three cuneiforms and the cuboid (with the metatarsal bases), highest at the intermediate cuneiform; both sides.

items.section: Ankle and Foot Joints and Supporting Structures
items.note: plantar fascia from SRC_Z_CALCANEUS_* tuberosity over SRC_Z_FLEXOR_DIGITORUM_BREVIS_* to the toes
items.custom_note: Thick central plantar fascia from the medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity forwards over flexor digitorum brevis, splitting into digital slips at the metatarsal heads (drawn on the plantar surface of FDB); both sides.

items.section: Ankle and Foot Joints and Supporting Structures
items.note: sustentaculum tali of SRC_Z_CALCANEUS_* to plantar SRC_Z_NAVICULAR_BONE_*
items.custom_note: Thick band from the sustentaculum tali to the plantar surface of the navicular, supporting the head of the talus from below (key static support of the medial longitudinal arch); both sides.

items.section: Ankle and Foot Joints and Supporting Structures
items.note: plantar SRC_Z_CALCANEUS_* to SRC_Z_CUBOID_BONE_* (short) and metatarsal bases (long); bodyparts has long plantar FJ1424/FJ1424M only
items.custom_note: Short plantar (plantar calcaneocuboid) ligament: wide short band from the anterior tubercle of the calcaneus to the plantar cuboid, deep to the long plantar ligament; both sides.

items.section: Ankle and Foot Joints and Supporting Structures
items.note: medial malleolus (SRC_Z_TIBIA_*) to medial SRC_Z_CALCANEUS_*; ankle retinacula not in z-anatomy
items.custom_note: Band of deep fascia from the medial malleolus to the medial surface of the calcaneus, roofing the tarsal tunnel over the tibialis posterior, FDL, posterior tibial vessels, tibial nerve and FHL; both sides. (Ankle retinacula are not in z-anatomy.)

items.section: Ankle and Foot Joints and Supporting Structures
items.note: deep to flexor retinaculum behind medial malleolus; contains SRC_Z_TIBIALIS_POSTERIOR_MUSCLE_*, SRC_Z_FLEXOR_DIGITORUM_LONGUS_*, SRC_Z_POSTERIOR_TIBIAL_ARTERY_*, SRC_Z_FLEXOR_HALLUCIS_LONGUS_*
items.custom_note: Space deep to the flexor retinaculum, between it and the medial talus/calcaneus behind the medial malleolus (drawn a little beyond the retinaculum so it shows); transmits tibialis posterior, FDL, posterior tibial vessels, tibial nerve, FHL; both sides.

Regional Nerves
items.note: no lower-limb nerves in z-anatomy; course: popliteal fossa along biceps femoris, round neck of SRC_Z_FIBULA_*
items.custom_note: From the sciatic bifurcation along the medial border of biceps femoris, behind the fibular head and round the fibular neck (subcutaneous here: foot drop when injured), dividing into deep and superficial branches; both sides.

items.section: Regional Nerves
items.note: no lower-limb nerves in z-anatomy; runs with SRC_Z_ANTERIOR_TIBIAL_ARTERY_* to SRC_Z_DORSALIS_PEDIS_ARTERY_*
items.custom_note: Branch of the common fibular nerve into the anterior compartment, down the interosseous membrane with the real anterior tibial artery, then lateral to dorsalis pedis to the first web space; both sides.

items.section: Regional Nerves
items.note: no lower-limb nerves in z-anatomy; lateral compartment between SRC_Z_FIBULARIS_LONGUS_MUSCLE_* and SRC_Z_EXTENSOR_DIGITORUM_LONGUS_*
items.custom_note: Branch of the common fibular nerve down the lateral compartment between the fibularis muscles and EDL (supplies fibularis longus/brevis), piercing the deep fascia in the distal leg to supply the skin of the dorsum of the foot; both sides.

items.section: Regional Nerves
items.note: no lower-limb nerves in z-anatomy; runs with SRC_Z_POPLITEAL_ARTERY_* then SRC_Z_POSTERIOR_TIBIAL_ARTERY_*
items.custom_note: From the sciatic bifurcation at the apex of the popliteal fossa, superficial to the popliteal vessels, deep to soleus with the real posterior tibial artery, behind the medial malleolus into the tarsal tunnel where it divides into the plantar nerves; both sides. (Lower-limb nerves are not in z-anatomy.)

items.section: Regional Nerves
items.note: no lower-limb nerves in z-anatomy; run with SRC_Z_MEDIAL_PLANTAR_ARTERY_* / SRC_Z_LATERAL_PLANTAR_ARTERY_*
items.custom_note: Larger terminal branch of the tibial nerve: forwards between abductor hallucis and FDB with the real medial plantar artery, ending as digital nerves to the medial 3.5 toes; both sides.

items.section: Regional Nerves
items.note: no lower-limb nerves in z-anatomy; runs with SRC_Z_GREAT_SAPHENOUS_VEIN_* in the leg
items.custom_note: Cutaneous terminal branch of the femoral nerve: subcutaneous at the medial knee, down the medial leg with the real great saphenous vein, anterior to the medial malleolus to the medial side of the foot; both sides.

items.section: Regional Nerves
items.note: no lower-limb nerves in z-anatomy; runs with SRC_Z_SMALL_SAPHENOUS_VEIN_*
items.custom_note: Cutaneous nerve (tibial + common fibular contributions) descending the posterior calf with the real small saphenous vein, behind the lateral malleolus to the lateral border of the foot and little toe; both sides.

items.section: Regional Arteries
items.note: diamond behind the knee bounded by gastrocnemius heads (SRC_Z_*_HEAD_OF_GASTROCNEMIUS_*), biceps femoris and semimembranosus; contains SRC_Z_POPLITEAL_ARTERY_*, SRC_Z_POPLITEAL_VEIN_*
items.custom_note: Diamond-shaped space behind the knee: biceps femoris (superolateral), semimembranosus/semitendinosus (superomedial), the two heads of gastrocnemius (inferior); floor = popliteal surface of femur, knee capsule, popliteus. Contains popliteal artery/vein, tibial and common fibular nerves; both sides.
